com.naver.linewebtoon.signInSdk: androidx Credential Manager (Play services provider) and Facebook Login

launch.evidence: Splash then the login screen (Continue with Email / Google / Facebook) rendered; the first frame of the login screen appeared only after another event (frame lag).

google_account_selection.evidence: Continue with Google -> Credential Manager found no framework credential service and used Play services (androidx.credentials HiddenActivity -> GIS PendingIntent). 'Choose an account to continue to WEBTOON' listed the test account; selecting it returned RESULT_OK.

google_tokens.evidence: The broker issued two OAuth tokens and an ID token for WEBTOON's server client ID (google_server_app_id) and granted the session.

google_sign_in.gap: After the credential reached the app, WEBTOON showed 'Login with your Google account failed.' WEBTOON made no further Play services call; its own login step (server) refused or failed. Cause open (not observable without the app's network trace).
google_sign_in.rerun: Rerun on 2026-11-21 board time (HKT) with both fixes: same "Login with your Google account failed." after Play services returned RESULT_OK to androidx.credentials HiddenActivity. Not the descriptor bugs; open.
google_sign_in.analysis: WEBTOON's handler for the Credential Manager result (GoogleLoginActivity) parses the Google ID token credential and then calls the Authorization API (Identity.getAuthorizationClient(activity).authorize: email and profile scopes, offline access, the chosen account); the dialog comes from that call's failure listener. Whether the request reaches Play services is not established yet. Play services logged WL-AUTH-PROXY package_accounts count=0 for WEBTOON, but in the same second as the broker issued the picker's tokens, so it belongs to the picker flow.
google_sign_in.cause: Found with WESTLAKE_PLAY_TRACE=1 (2026-11-21 board time): after the ID token reaches WEBTOON, its Authorization API call asks Play services for service 219 and gets status 9 (SERVICE_INVALID). Play services refuses the service to uncertified devices; 219 is not on the approved exception list (212, 213, 91, 44, 5, 29). The sign-in service 212 answered status 0. Uncertified-device policy, not a Westlake gap, unless the user approves adding 219.
google_sign_in.after_219: With 219 added to the eligibility list (363a071, framework v27 on Play services, 2026-11-21 board time): service 219 answers status 0 and WEBTOON calls IAuthorizationService.authorize, which calls back. The login still fails. During the authorize step Play services asked for WEBTOON's accounts twice and got none (WL-AUTH-PROXY package_accounts count=0), and no token request reached the broker. Next gap: the chosen account is visible to an app only while its picker is open or while Play services serves its synchronous call. The asynchronous Authorization API needs the same mediation as the legacy asynchronous sign-in (GoogleAsyncAuthOperations), including the server auth code.
google_sign_in.after_experiments: Observed on 2026-11-21 board time (HKT) with four user-approved experiments on Play services (framework v34): the Google sign-in completed, WEBTOON's sign-up took the test defaults (birthday 1 Jan 1990, nickname; marketing emails left unchecked), and MainActivity and the MY tab rendered. The chain that had to be cleared, in order: (1) service 219 refused by the uncertified gate (added, 363a071); (2) Play services saw no account for WEBTOON during the asynchronous authorize call (lease for the app's own live request, WESTLAKE_GOOGLE_ASYNC_AUTHORIZATION); (3) the Sign in with Google credential named the account by its numeric ID, because Play services' own account-details sync (MdiSync, service 215) is refused on the uncertified board and its sign-in UI falls back to partial data; Play services then refused that account (internal code 28433); the request now names the granted account when the ID is exactly that account's Google ID (WESTLAKE_GOOGLE_AUTHORIZATION_ACCOUNT_ID); (4) the server auth code for the request was withheld in Play services' :persistent, which made Play services ask for re-authentication (updateCredentials, unsupported); it is now delegated for the live request only, pinned to the app, signer, named account and server client ID (WESTLAKE_GOOGLE_AUTHORIZATION_TOKENS). Also on during the pass: Play services' own tokens for four account-management scopes (WESTLAKE_GOOGLE_BROKER_SELF_TOKENS) and 215 on the exception list; both were on, and whether the pass needs either was not tested.

facebook_sign_in.evidence: On 2026-11-21 board time (HKT) with both fixes: Continue with Facebook -> FacebookLoginActivity -> FacebookActivity -> CustomTabMainActivity -> Facebook's web login; Facebook showed a reCAPTCHA ("I'm not a robot"), which the user solved on the board; NAVER's NeoIdTokenLoginActivity returned RESULT_OK to LoginActivity; SignUpActivity took the test defaults (birthday 1 Jan 1990, nickname) and Agree & Sign up; interest onboarding skipped; MainActivity (home) and the MY tab rendered.

google_tokens.evidence: Join for free -> Sign up with Google, and separately Log In -> Google: Play services' picker offered the test account; the broker issued an OAuth token, an ID token and a server auth code for Strava's server client ID, granted the session, and RESULT_OK reached LogInOrSignUpActivity both times.

google_sign_in.gap: Both times Strava then started SplashActivity, which routed back to the welcome carousel (not signed in). No exception, network error, toast or AccountManager call was logged; Strava also binds Play Integrity (express) through the Play Store. Cause open; an app/server-side check failing on this uncertified board is a hypothesis, not established.
google_sign_in.rerun: Rerun on 2026-11-21 board time (HKT) with both fixes: the sign-up/log-in window now attached at once; the account pick returned RESULT_OK to LogInOrSignUpActivity, a progress dialog showed, then SplashActivity -> welcome carousel again. google_sign_in.trace: With WESTLAKE_PLAY_TRACE=1 (2026-11-21 board time): after RESULT_OK reaches LogInOrSignUpActivity, Strava makes no further Play services service request, so no gate refusal. It had sent two Play Integrity requests to the Play Store (IExpressIntegrityService code 2, one-way). The Store bound ExpressIntegrityService but no callback ever reached Strava. Strava then went Splash -> welcome. Lead: the Store does not answer express integrity requests. Even an answer would carry failing verdicts on this uncertified board.
google_sign_in.integrity: Rerun on 2026-11-21 board time (HKT) with the Store traced and its log captured privately. The Store now answers Strava's two express-integrity warm-up requests: it generates a key attestation record and asks play-fe for intermediate integrity, then calls Strava back twice (IExpressIntegrityServiceCallback code 2). On the way it asks Play services for service 370, PLAY_INTEGRITY_API, and the uncertified gate refuses it (status 9). After the account pick (RESULT_OK), Strava requests no integrity token, reads the advertising ID, and restarts at Splash, landing on the welcome carousel logged out. Its preferences show no saved login. The earlier 'Store never answers' was not reproduced. The block is the Play Integrity restriction, which ADR-0010 keeps out of scope. Allowing 370 would only produce an honest failing device-integrity verdict on this uncertified board, so it was not tried.

westlakeFixes.f46ae1b: Window shim: perform(NATIVE_WINDOW_GET_LAST_QUEUED_BUFFER/_2) now writes no buffer and fence -1 before its error. hwui's PixelCopy readback (Readback::copySurfaceInto) closes that fence on every return path, so the unwritten value closed whatever its stack held: another thread's descriptor when that number was open. Root cause of Duolingo's in-app browser aborts ([FATAL:scoped_file.cc(43)] and [FATAL:udp_socket_posix.cc(276)] Bad file descriptor) and of its RenderThread Looper POLL_ERROR. Found with a kernel trace of fd_install and every close with its user-space caller; the fixed run had no descriptor closed by anyone but its owner across about a million traced events.
westlakeFixes.876034c-deployment: The runtime deployed for this stack (8e5d7304) was built from a worktree without westlake 876034c (the input receiver keeps its own duplicate of the channel descriptor), so each window teardown closed one descriptor number twice. Rebuilt byte-for-byte from the recorded command with only that change: cef91a38.
